column1: SECTION B — LESSON PLAN FIDELITY   |   Fidelity Score = (actions observed ÷ actions prescribed) × 100%   |   ≥85% High | 60–84% Medium | <60% Low

column3: No clear learning objective stated. Activities lack purpose.
column4: Objective mentioned but vague or not referenced during lesson.
column5: Clear objective stated, referred to during lesson, linked to classroom activities.
column6: Objective co-constructed with students, revisited at close. Students can articulate what they are learning and why.
column8:
FICO V3 (B1) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + HOTS Lesson Planning ('Objectives explicitly link to critical thinking')

Why: When teachers state objectives clearly, students show 15–20% higher task completion. HOTS rubric requires explicit HOTS-linked objectives.

column4: Some structure but missing key phases (intro/body/close).
column5: Clear I Do → We Do → You Do sequence. Logical flow with transitions.
column6: Logical flow with smooth transitions, recap, and closure activity. Students can follow the arc.
column8:
FICO V3 (B8) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + OECD (Structured Lesson)

Why: Structured lessons improve retention by ~25% (Rosenshine). Sequence ensures cognitive load is managed progressively.

column4: Some activities align but others are filler.
column5: Most activities directly support the learning objective.
column6: All activities purposefully scaffolded toward objective mastery. No wasted time.
column8:
FICO V3 (B3) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + HOTS Lesson Planning ('Strategies for promoting analysis, evaluation, synthesis')

Why: Alignment between objectives and activities is the strongest predictor of lesson effectiveness (Hattie, d=0.56).

column3: No reference to what students already know.
column4: Brief mention but no student input sought.
column5: Teacher connects new content to previously taught material.
column6: Students actively recall and link prior knowledge; teacher builds on it.
column8:
FICO V3 (B4) + OECD (Cognitive Activation) + HOTS (Remember/Understand level)

Why: Schema activation makes new learning 'stick' — Ausubel's meaningful learning theory. Critical for low-resource contexts.

column3: Content presented in isolation, no real-world link.
column4: Teacher mentions a connection but doesn't develop it.
column5: Content connected to students' lives or local context.
column6: Students generate their own connections; examples from their community.
column8:
FICO V3 (B5) + OECD (Cognitive Activation) + HOTS Lesson Planning ('Lesson integrates interdisciplinary or real-world applications')

Why: HOTS rubric explicitly requires real-world integration. Contextual relevance increases motivation and transfer in Pakistani classrooms.

column4: Aware of different levels but no adapted tasks.
column5: Tasks differentiated for at least 2 ability groups.
column6: Multiple pathways offered; struggling students supported, advanced students stretched.
column8:
FICO V3 (B6) + TEACH (Checks for Understanding) + OECD (Differentiation) + Training Curriculum (Inclusive Education domain)

Why: In multi-grade Pakistani classrooms, differentiation is survival. Linked to reduced dropout rates.

column3: Taleemabad lesson plan not used at all.
column4: Plan open but teacher deviates significantly.
column5: Plan followed with minor contextual adaptations.
column6: Plan followed faithfully AND adapted intelligently to class needs.
column8:
FICO V3 (Original Fidelity Check)

Why: Core fidelity metric — measures whether the designed intervention is being delivered. Without this, impact evaluation is meaningless.

column3: No Taleemabad resources (video, worksheet, manipulatives) used.
column4: Some resources used but not as intended.
column5: Key resources used as prescribed in lesson plan.
column6: All resources used effectively; teacher adds complementary materials.
column8:
FICO V3 (Bi — Effective Resource Use) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation)

Why: Resources are the delivery mechanism of the curriculum. Fidelity to resource use = fidelity to pedagogical intent.

column2: Time on Task / Time on Learning
column3: Less than 50% of class time spent on learning activities.
column6: More than 85% on task; routines are automatic, transitions seamless.
column8:
TEACH (Time on Task — Area 1) + OECD (Classroom Management) + HOTS Observation Form (Time on Learning: L/M/H intervals)

Why: TEACH evidence: every 10% increase in time on task = measurable learning gains. Pakistani classrooms average ~55%.

column3: Lesson ends abruptly with no summary.
column4: Teacher rushes through a brief recap.
column5: Structured closure: recap key points, check understanding.
column6: Students summarize learning, connect to next lesson, self-assess.
column8:
FICO V3 (B8 Sequence) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation)

Why: Closure activates retrieval practice — the single most effective learning strategy (Dunlosky et al., 2013).
